summary: 49ers GM John Lynch confirmed Pearsall will undergo PCL reconstruction surgery, ending his 2026 season entirely. The lingering 2025 knee injury (first suffered Week 4 last season) "declared itself" during camp after the team opted against surgery in the offseason. A 2025-based per-game rate should not be used at all for a 2026 projection.

Re-signed with San Francisco on a one-year, $7M deal in early August. With Ricky Pearsall out for the season and Mike Evans-caliber depth thin behind him, Samuel projects for a larger target/touch share in the 49ers' offense than his most recent full season elsewhere suggested.

Sitting out of practice with leg "tightness" after already missing preseason action with an undisclosed injury. Nothing structural has been reported, but it's a second camp absence and worth monitoring into Week 1.

Currently an unsigned free agent recovering from a dislocated knee/torn ACL and other knee ligaments. Hill said in a personal video update he still has "no power" in his left leg; whether he plays anywhere in 2026 at all is in real doubt. Not draftable off last season's per-game rate under any current NFL contract.

Arrested in May on domestic-abuse-related charges; the NFL's personal-conduct review is still pending as of late August, but a suspension is expected. The CBA's baseline for this offense is 6 games, which would cost him the Packers' games against MIN/NYJ/ATL/TB/CHI/DAL to open the 2026 season (opener is Sept. 13 vs. Minnesota). Still practicing with the team while the case is reviewed.

Rehabbing a ruptured Achilles suffered in the January 2026 playoffs, plus a camp groin issue. As of late August he says he feels "wonderful" and is expected to play Week 1 — a notably fast Achilles recovery, but still worth confirming closer to kickoff before trusting a full-workload 2026 projection.
Held out of practice with a hip injury; Dan Campbell called it "aggravated" but said the team feels good long-term, while declining to guarantee he's ready for the regular-season opener.

Named Cleveland's Week 1 starter over Shedeur Sanders on Aug. 24, despite preseason accuracy/completion charting favoring Sanders throughout camp — the $86M 2026 dead-cap hit behind Watson's contract was reportedly a deciding factor. Secures the job, at least to open the season.

Lost the Week 1 starting job to Deshaun Watson on Aug. 24 despite reportedly outplaying him on efficiency/accuracy metrics through camp and preseason — the decision leaned on Watson's contract investment, not performance. Opens the season as Cleveland's backup with no clear path to snaps unless Watson struggles or is hurt.

Former Giants HC Brian Daboll is Tennessee's new playcaller for 2026, and reshaped the receiving corps around Ward accordingly: drafted WR Carnell Tate 4th overall, signed slot WR Wan'Dale Robinson (who produced in Daboll's Giants offense) in free agency, and gets a healthy Calvin Ridley back. None of last season's target distribution for this offense carries forward unchanged.

Enters 2026 as Tennessee's likely WR3, not WR1 — rookie Carnell Tate (4th overall) projects to take the downfield role and free-agent addition Wan'Dale Robinson (8.2 targets/game in Daboll's scheme with the Giants) projects to take the underneath/slot volume. His limited, injury-shortened 2025 (7 games, no TDs) is a poor baseline for 2026 regardless.

Titans' 4th overall pick out of Ohio State; zero drops and an FBS-leading contested-catch rate (12/14) in his final college season. Has a clear path to the downfield/No. 1 receiver role as a rookie in Brian Daboll's new offense — projects as a low-end WR2, a role no historical stat line for him exists to project from.

Left the Giants in free agency to reunite with new Titans playcaller Brian Daboll, who fed him 8.2 targets/game over his last 38 games together. Projects as Tennessee's clear WR2/underneath volume option — his prior team-context numbers (Giants offense, different QB) don't carry over, but the scheme role does.

Traded from New England to Houston on Aug. 24 (for S Jaylen Reed + a 2028 7th) after the Patriots got crowded at WR by adding A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Boutte had requested the trade; a clean-slate role in Houston's receiver room replaces whatever target share he'd have gotten buried behind Brown/Doubs in New England.

Signed by Detroit as the clear backup to Jahmyr Gibbs after the Lions traded David Montgomery to Houston in the offseason — last season's Lions backfield split (Gibbs/Montgomery) no longer applies. Has also been limited in camp by a sprained MCL; Dan Campbell says he "feels pretty good" about Pacheco being ready to open the season.
Hyperextended his knee in practice and is expected to miss multiple weeks; his Week 1 availability is in doubt.
Positioned for a bigger share of Chicago's backfield work if Kyle Monangai's hyperextended knee (see separate note) keeps him out into the regular season.
Activated off the PUP list on Aug. 27, with the stated goal of being ready for Week 1.
Appears on track to play Week 1 in the Giants' new offense — an improved outlook from earlier-August injury concerns. Talent and role make him a real value pick if he opens the season healthy.
Waived by Arizona on Aug. 24 after a second straight injury-limited camp (knee, following meniscus surgery) and a crowded backfield behind him. Now a free agent with no current NFL role.

Arizona's backfield thinned out fast this camp: Trey Benson was waived (see separate note) and rookie 1st-rounder Jeremiyah Love has been dealing with an ankle issue. Allgeier is positioned as a real early-season complementary/lead-back option behind whichever of Arizona's backs are healthy, a bigger role than his career usage elsewhere implies.

The NFL has concluded Rice will not face a suspension for his offseason legal issues (a probation violation tied to a positive THC test, which the league no longer suspends for) or for separate conduct allegations. Removes the suspension risk that shadowed his offseason — full Week 1 workload now expected.

3rd-round rookie (USC) drawing consistent praise from Ravens beat reporters through camp — physical, tough to guard downfield and in the red zone. Speculative camp buzz on a depth WR, worth a late-round dynasty/best-ball look rather than a redraft priority.

Rookie TE getting notably strong praise for athleticism and reliable hands out of Patriots camp. TE is a thin value position; worth flagging as a late-round dynasty stash even with no proven NFL role yet.

Browns 1st-round rookie WR flashed with a big catch-and-run touchdown in the preseason opener vs. Chicago and said his confidence "skyrocketed" afterward. Early, small-sample preseason signal, not a resolved role.
